  main                   4add51d [origin/main] 2.3.3: CI reliability: retry transient network failures in the JS image build and remove a SIGPIPE false-negative from the dind example tests (issue #104 / PR #105). The JS image build (`ubuntu/24.04/js/install.sh`, `COPY`'d into every dind/language image) occasionally died on a single transient third-party error, with no retry: the lean/language build hit a flaky npm registry response during `npm install -g npm@latest`, and the dind-swift build hit `playwright install … msedge …` getting an invalid GPG key body from packages.microsoft.com ("gpg: no valid OpenPGP data found" → "Failed to install msedge"). Every network-bound build step — the npm self-update, the Playwright/Puppeteer CLI install, and the Playwright browser-binary download — now goes through a `run_with_retry` wrapper that retries with exponential backoff (mirroring `apt_update_with_retry` in `common.sh`, with the same overridable retry budget so it stays unit-testable). `playwright install` skips already-present browsers, so a retry only re-attempts the one that blipped. This is build-time resilience only — the resulting image is unchanged on success. Separately, the dind example suite asserted on container logs with `docker logs … | grep -q "needle"`. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in `docs/dind/USAGE.md`.

Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in `docs/dind/USAGE.md`.

box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

The JS image build (`ubuntu/24.04/js/install.sh`, `COPY`'d into every dind/language image) occasionally died on a single transient third-party error, with no retry: the lean/language build hit a flaky npm registry response during `npm install -g npm@latest`, and the dind-swift build hit `playwright install … msedge …` getting an invalid GPG key body from packages.microsoft.com (\"gpg: no valid OpenPGP data found\" → \"Failed to install msedge\"). Every network-bound build step — the npm self-update, the Playwright/Puppeteer CLI install, and the Playwright browser-binary download — now goes through a `run_with_retry` wrapper that retries with exponential backoff (mirroring `apt_update_with_retry` in `common.sh`, with the same overridable retry budget so it stays unit-testable). `playwright install` skips already-present browsers, so a retry only re-attempts the one that blipped. This is build-time resilience only — the resulting image is unchanged on success. Separately, the dind example suite asserted on container logs with `docker logs … | grep -q \"needle\"`. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in `docs/dind/USAGE.md`.\n4f67188 Merge pull request #105 from link-foundation/issue-104-8849a1f71a19\n55e2efa js CI: retry the Playwright browser install to survive a transient msedge GPG flake (issue #104)\n3958614 dind/js CI: kill two transient build/test flakes (issue #104)\n5b9944e dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the vfs storage driver (issue #104)\n13d4c05 Initial commit with task details\ne51b58d 2.3.2: dind-box: warn when host-image passthrough is opted into but no host socket is mounted (issue #102). Running `box-dind` with passthrough enabled (the default `public` mode) **and** an explicit allowlist (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=...`) but **without** the host Docker socket bind-mounted used to be a silent no-op: the entrypoint copied nothing, printed nothing, and the first nested `docker run` re-pulled the full image from the registry with no hint why. Downstream this re-pulled a 30+ GB image because of a forgotten `-v` flag (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). A non-empty `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is an unambiguous opt-in signal, so `passthrough_host_images` now emits a single actionable warning in exactly that case — enabled passthrough + allowlist set + no socket mounted — naming the missing `-v /var/run/docker.sock:${DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK}:ro` mount. The present-but-unreachable socket already warned and still does; plain `box-dind` containers that never set an allowlist stay silent so the default mode is not spammed. The existing `setup-buildx-resilient` pre-pull (issue #97) only retries Docker Hub, so once the outage outlasted its retry budget the boot pull failed too — and that single failure cascaded into `box-java:<ver>-amd64: not found` and `box:<ver>-{amd64,arm64}: not found` across `build-dind-amd64 (java)`, `build-dind-amd64 (full)` and `build-dind-arm64 (full)`. `setup-buildx-resilient` now falls back to a pull-through registry mirror (`mirror.gcr.io`, on independent infrastructure) and re-tags the BuildKit image to its canonical reference so the docker-container driver boot reuses the local copy and never touches the failing registry. Adds an opt-in `verbose` / `RUNNER_DEBUG` trace and a unit test (`experiments/test-issue100-buildx-mirror-fallback.sh`). All 12 buildx boots in `release.yml` route through this one composite action, so every build job is hardened. [2026-06-19T10:33:22.042Z] [INFO]       "content": "### Scoping to specific images (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`)\n\nThe mode gate decides *whether* an image is safe to pass; the registry allowlist\nnarrows it *by registry host*. `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is one level finer\n— it scopes passthrough to **specific repositories / image names**. When it is\nnon-empty, a host image must match the mode filter **and** at least one\nspace-separated pattern; empty (the default) keeps the mode + registry behavior.\n\nThis is the precise fit for \"seed the inner daemon with only the images I own\"\nrather than every public host image:\n\n```bash\n# Pass through only hive-mind's own images, nothing else on the host:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=public \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=\"konard/hive-mind konard/hive-mind-dind\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\n# Globs and explicit tags / registry-qualified refs also work:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=\"docker.io/konard/hive-mind* konard/hive-mind-dind:latest\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nPatterns are matched against several normalized forms of each host image\nreference, so a bare repository like `konard/hive-mind` matches the tagged\n`konard/hive-mind:latest` and the registry-qualified\n`docker.io/konard/hive-mind:latest` alike. Because it composes with the mode\ngate, `public` mode still refuses a locally-built or private image even when it\nmatches a pattern — the allowlist only ever *narrows* the eligible set, it never\nwidens it past the security filter.\n\nSetting `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is an unambiguous \"I expect these images\npassed through\" signal. So if it is set but **no host socket is mounted**, the\nentrypoint no longer stays silent — it emits a single warning naming the\nmissing `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro` mount, because\nthe nested daemon will otherwise re-pull from the registry on the first\n`docker run` with no hint as to why (issue #102). Plain `box-dind` containers\nthat never set an allowlist still see no extra noise when no socket is mounted.\n\n## Commit Cycles\n\n`DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1` is useful for setup containers where you want to install or\nconfigure files before committing an image:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name box-dind-setup \\\n  -e DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1 \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\ndocker exec box-dind-setup bash -lc 'echo setup complete'\ndocker commit --change 'ENV DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=0' box-dind-setup my-box-dind\ndocker run -d --privileged --name my-box-dind my-box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nThe `--change 'ENV DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=0'` reset is intentional. This is build-time resilience only — the resulting image is unchanged on success. Separately, the dind example suite asserted on container logs with `docker logs … | grep -q \"needle\"`. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Running `box-dind` with passthrough enabled (the default `public` mode) **and** an explicit allowlist (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=...`) but **without** the host Docker socket bind-mounted used to be a silent no-op: the entrypoint copied nothing, printed nothing, and the first nested `docker run` re-pulled the full image from the registry with no hint why. Downstream this re-pulled a 30+ GB image because of a forgotten `-v` flag (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). A non-empty `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is an unambiguous opt-in signal, so `passthrough_host_images` now emits a single actionable warning in exactly that case — enabled passthrough + allowlist set + no socket mounted — naming the missing `-v /var/run/docker.sock:${DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK}:ro` mount. Run 27314587149 failed not from a code defect but from `registry-1.docker.io` being unreachable for ~2.5 minutes while booting BuildKit in `build-languages-amd64 (java)`. The existing `setup-buildx-resilient` pre-pull (issue #97) only retries Docker Hub, so once the outage outlasted its retry budget the boot pull failed too — and that single failure cascaded into `box-java:<ver>-amd64: not found` and `box:<ver>-{amd64,arm64}: not found` across `build-dind-amd64 (java)`, `build-dind-amd64 (full)` and `build-dind-arm64 (full)`. `setup-buildx-resilient` now falls back to a pull-through registry mirror (`mirror.gcr.io`, on independent infrastructure) and re-tags the BuildKit image to its canonical reference so the docker-container driver boot reuses the local copy and never touches the failing registry. Adds an opt-in `verbose` / `RUNNER_DEBUG` trace and a unit test (`experiments/test-issue100-buildx-mirror-fallback.sh`). All 12 buildx boots in `release.yml` route through this one composite action, so every build job is hardened. When non-empty, only host images whose reference matches at least one space-separated pattern (glob) are passed through, composed with the existing mode gate (so `public` still requires a public RepoDigest). The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. When a\n#                        host Docker socket is mounted into the container at\n#                        DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK, images already present on the\n#                        host are copied into the nested daemon at startup\n#                        (docker save | docker load) so they are not re-pulled.\n#                        Modes:\n#                          public - (default) only pass host images that carry a\n#                                   RepoDigest from an allowlisted public\n#                                   registry (DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES).\n#                                   These are freely re-pullable, so passing them\n#                                   leaks no local build secrets or private\n#                                   registry credentials.\n#                          all    - pass every tagged host image, including\n#                                   locally-built and private-registry images.\n#                          off    - disable passthrough entirely.\n#                        If no host socket is mounted this is a quiet no-op, so\n#                        the default is safe for the normal --privileged run.\n#                        (issue #94)\n#   DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK\n#                        Path inside the container to the mounted *host* Docker\n#                        socket used for passthrough (default:\n#                        /var/run/host-docker.sock). Mount it read-only with\n#                        `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro`.\n#                        Note: deliberately NOT /var/run/docker.sock, so the\n#                        inner daemon keeps its own isolated socket. Start the inner Docker daemon (dockerd) in the background with root\n#      privileges, using scoped passwordless sudo when the image runs as box.\n#   2. Wait for dockerd to be ready on /var/run/docker.sock.\n#   3. Hand off to the standard /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh so all language\n#      environments load exactly like in the regular box.\n#\n# This is the recommended pattern from docker:dind and cruizba/ubuntu-dind.\n# See docs/case-studies/issue-80/CASE-STUDY.md for the full design rationale.\n#\n# Required runtime privileges (host side):\n#   - Default:  docker run --privileged konard/<base>-dind\n#   - Sysbox :  docker run --runtime=sysbox-runc konard/<base>-dind   (no --privileged)\n#\n# Environment overrides:\n#   DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER  Override storage driver (default: auto-detected: overlay2,\n#                        fuse-overlayfs, vfs). Note: vfs has NO copy-on-write — it\n#                        stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so\n#                        large (multi-GB) images consume many times their size on\n#                        disk and 'docker pull'/'docker run' can fail with 'no\n#                        space left on device'. When the active driver ends up\n#                        being vfs the entrypoint emits a one-time warning naming\n#                        the fuse-overlayfs (copy-on-write) remediation. (issue #104)\n#   DIND_DATA_ROOT       Override --data-root for dockerd (default: /var/lib/docker)\n#   DIND_LOG_FILE        Where to write dockerd logs (default: /var/log/dockerd.log)\n#   DIND_WAIT_SECONDS    How long to wait for dockerd to come up (default: 30)\n#   DIND_SKIP_DAEMON     If set to \"1\", do not start dockerd (use for DooD/Sysbox-only mode)\n#   DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL Space-separated list of image tarball files and/or\n#                        directories to `docker load` into the nested daemon\n#                        once it is ready. Directories load every *.tar inside.\n#                        This is how you reuse host images without re-downloading\n#                        them: `docker save img | ... ` on the host, mount the\n#                        tarball, and point this at it. (issue #94)\n#   DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES  Space-separated list of image references to `docker pull`\n#                        into the nested daemon once it is ready, but only when\n#                        the image is not already present. Useful to warm the\n#                        cache from a registry or pull-through mirror. When a\n#                        host Docker socket is mounted into the container at\n#                        DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK, images already present on the\n#                        host are copied into the nested daemon at startup\n#                        (docker save | docker load) so they are not re-pulled.\n#                        Modes:\n#                          public - (default) only pass host images that carry a\n#                                   RepoDigest from an allowlisted public\n#                                   registry (DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES).\n#                                   These are freely re-pullable, so passing them\n#                                   leaks no local build secrets or private\n#                                   registry credentials.\n#                          all    - pass every tagged host image, including\n#                                   locally-built and private-registry images.\n#                          off    - disable passthrough entirely.\n#                        If no host socket is mounted this is a quiet no-op, so\n#                        the default is safe for the normal --privileged run.\n#                        (issue #94)\n#   DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK\n#                        Path inside the container to the mounted *host* Docker\n#                        socket used for passthrough (default:\n#                        /var/run/host-docker.sock). Mount it read-only with\n#                        `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro`.\n#                        Note: deliberately NOT /var/run/docker.sock, so the\n#                        inner daemon keeps its own isolated socket. (issue #94)\n#   DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES\n#                        Space-separated allowlist of registries treated as\n#                        \"public\" in DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=public mode (default:\n#                        the common public registries: docker.io ghcr.io quay.io\n#                        gcr.io registry.k8s.io public.ecr.aws mcr.microsoft.com).\n#                        (issue #94)\n#   DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES\n#                        Space-separated allowlist of image references / globs.\n#                        When non-empty, only host images whose reference matches\n#                        at least one entry are passed through, composed with the\n#                        mode filter (so \"public\" still gates on a public\n#                        RepoDigest). Empty/unset keeps the current behavior\n#                        (mode + registry filter only). Patterns are matched\n#                        against several normalized forms of the reference, so\n#                        \"konard/hive-mind\" matches \"konard/hive-mind:latest\" and\n#                        \"docker.io/konard/hive-mind:latest\" alike, and globs work\n#                        (e.g. \"docker.io/konard/hive-mind*\"). This narrows\n#                        passthrough one level finer than the registry allowlist\n#                        — to specific repositories / image names. (issue #97)\n#                        After passthrough runs, every *concrete* entry here (an\n#                        explicit tag or digest, no glob) is verified to actually\n#                        be present in the nested daemon; a missing one triggers a\n#                        loud warning instead of a false \"complete\", because the\n#                        first nested 'docker run' would otherwise silently re-pull\n#                        the multi-GB image from the registry (the lingering\n#                        symptom of issues #94 / #102, still seen downstream in\n#                        link-assistant/hive-mind#1914/#1946). [2026-06-19T10:40:55.910Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "# dind-box Usage\n\nThe `-dind` images are regular box images with Docker Engine added. They keep the\nsame user-facing default as the non-dind images: `docker exec` opens as `box`\nwith `HOME=/home/box`. The entrypoint starts the inner `dockerd` with a scoped\npasswordless sudo rule, then hands off to the normal box entrypoint.\n\nThe runnable examples in this document live under `tests/dind/` and are executed\nby pull request CI against the locally built `box-dind-js` image.\n\n## Runtime Flags\n\nUse one of these host-side runtime modes when you need the inner Docker daemon:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged --name box-dind konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --runtime=sysbox-runc --name box-dind konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\n`--privileged` is the default Docker-in-Docker mode. Sysbox is the preferred\nmode for shared hosts when the `sysbox-runc` runtime is installed, because it is\ndesigned for system containers without exposing the host Docker socket.\n\nWithout a runtime that lets the inner daemon create namespaces, mounts, and\ncgroups, the container shell can still start but Docker commands normally fail:\n\n```text\n[dind-entrypoint] WARN: dockerd did not become ready within 30s\nCannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock\n```\n\nThe dockerd log path is controlled by `DIND_LOG_FILE` and defaults to\n`/var/log/dockerd.log`.\n\n## Basic Docker Use\n\nThis example starts the image, waits for the entrypoint to bring up the inner\ndaemon, and checks that `docker exec` still lands as `box`:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged --name box-dind konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\nuntil docker exec box-dind docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do\n  sleep 1\ndone\n\ndocker exec box-dind whoami\ndocker exec box-dind docker ps\ndocker exec box-dind pgrep -x dockerd\n```\n\nCI runs the same flow as an executable example:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-basic-docker-ps.sh\n```\n\n## Runtime Environment\n\nThe entrypoint supports these environment variables:\n\n| Variable | Default | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` | auto | Override the inner dockerd storage driver. |\n| `DIND_DATA_ROOT` | `/var/lib/docker` | Override the inner dockerd data root. |\n| `DIND_LOG_FILE` | `/var/log/dockerd.log` | Write dockerd logs to this path. |\n| `DIND_WAIT_SECONDS` | `30` | Wait this many seconds for dockerd readiness. |\n| `DIND_SKIP_DAEMON` | `0` | Set to `1` to skip dockerd startup. |\n| `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` | _(empty)_ | Space-separated `docker save` tarballs and/or directories of `*.tar` to `docker load` into the nested daemon once it is ready. |\n| `DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES` | _(empty)_ | Space-separated image references to `docker pull` into the nested daemon once it is ready, skipping any that are already present. |\n| `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH` | `public` | Copy images already present on the host into the nested daemon at startup when a host socket is mounted (see below). `public` only passes images with a RepoDigest from an allowlisted public registry; `all` passes every tagged image; `off` disables it. A quiet no-op when no host socket is mounted. |\n| `DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK` | `/var/run/host-docker.sock` | Path inside the container to the mounted *host* Docker socket used for passthrough. Deliberately **not** `/var/run/docker.sock`, so the inner daemon keeps its own isolated socket. |\n| `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES` | common public registries | Space-separated allowlist of registries treated as \"public\" in `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=public` mode (default: `docker.io ghcr.io quay.io gcr.io registry.k8s.io public.ecr.aws mcr.microsoft.com`). |\n| `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` | _(empty)_ | Space-separated allowlist of image references / globs. When non-empty, only host images matching at least one entry are passed through, composed with the mode filter (so `public` still requires a public RepoDigest). Empty keeps the mode + registry filter only. One level finer than `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES` — scope to specific repositories / image names. |\n\nUse a named volume when the inner Docker state should survive container removal:\n\n```bash\ndocker volume create box-dind-data\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v box-dind-data:/var/lib/docker \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\n## Reusing Host Images (Preload)\n\nThe nested daemon starts with an **empty image store**. By default a\n`docker run <image>` *inside* the container reports\n`Unable to find image '<image>' locally` and pulls a fresh copy from the\nregistry — even when the host daemon already has that exact image (issue #94).\nThis is the well-known [Docker-in-Docker image-cache pitfall][jpetazzo].\n\nThe entrypoint can seed the nested daemon at startup so no re-download happens.\n\n### `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` — load `docker save` tarballs (reuse host images)\n\nOn the host, save the image you already have to a tarball, mount it into the\ncontainer, and point `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` at it. The entrypoint loads it with\n`docker load` as soon as the inner daemon is ready, before your workload runs:\n\n```bash\n# Host already has the image; export it without a registry round-trip:\ndocker pull alpine:3.20\ndocker save alpine:3.20 -o /tmp/preload/alpine.tar\n\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /tmp/preload:/preload:ro \\\n  -e DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL=/preload/alpine.tar \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\nuntil docker exec box-dind docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done\n\n# No \"Unable to find image locally\" — it was preloaded, not pulled:\ndocker exec box-dind docker run --rm alpine:3.20 echo hi\n```\n\n`DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` accepts a space-separated list. Any entry that is a\ndirectory loads every `*.tar` file inside it, so you can mount a whole folder of\nsaved images:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /tmp/preload:/preload:ro \\\n  -e DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL=/preload \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nYou can also bake a tarball into a derived image so every container starts warm:\n\n```dockerfile\nFROM konard/box-dind\nUSER root\nCOPY images.tar /opt/preload/images.tar\nENV DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL=/opt/preload/images.tar\nUSER box\nENV HOME=/home/box\n```\n\n### `DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES` — warm the cache from a registry\n\nWhen the source is a registry or pull-through mirror rather than a tarball, list\nthe references in `DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES`. The entrypoint pulls each one after the\ndaemon is ready, but skips any image that is already present (for example one a\nmounted `/var/lib/docker` volume or a `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` already provided):\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES=\"alpine:3.20 busybox:1.36\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nPreload failures are non-fatal: the entrypoint logs a warning and continues so\nthe container shell still starts. Preload is skipped entirely when\n`DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1`, since there is no inner daemon to load into.\n\nCI covers this behavior here:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh\n```\n\n[jpetazzo]: https://jpetazzo.github.io/2015/09/03/do-not-use-docker-in-docker-for-ci/\n\n## Host-Image Passthrough (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH`)\n\n`DIND_PRELOAD_*` above are explicit: you name the tarballs or references to seed.\nPassthrough is the **automatic** counterpart — when you mount the host Docker\nsocket into the container, the entrypoint copies images the host *already has*\ninto the nested daemon at startup, so the inner `docker run` does not re-pull\nthem. It is on by default (`public` mode) but a quiet no-op until a host socket\nis mounted, so the standard `--privileged` run is unchanged.\n\nMount the host socket at `DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK` (default\n`/var/run/host-docker.sock`), read-only:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\nuntil docker exec box-dind docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done\n\n# Public host images were copied into the inner daemon — no re-pull:\ndocker exec box-dind docker images\n```\n\nThe mount path is deliberately **not** `/var/run/docker.sock`. The host socket is\nread only at startup to *seed* images; the inner daemon keeps its own isolated\nsocket and remains the container's runtime. This preserves the per-container\nDocker view from issue #80 — mounting the host socket at the default path would\nswitch the model to Docker-outside-of-Docker and expose host Docker control\n(see [Host Prerequisites](#host-prerequisites)).\n\n### Modes — and why `public` is the default\n\n| Mode | What it copies |\n| --- | --- |\n| `public` _(default)_ | Only host images carrying a `RepoDigest` from an allowlisted public registry (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES`). A RepoDigest proves the image was pulled from that registry and is freely re-pullable, so copying it leaks **no** local build secrets and needs **no** registry credential. Locally-built images (no RepoDigest) and private-registry images are skipped. |\n| `all` | Every tagged host image, including locally-built and private-registry images. Use only when you trust the inner workload with those images. |\n| `off` (also `0`/`false`/`no`) | Disable passthrough entirely. |\n\n```bash\n# Pass through everything the host has, including local builds:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\n# Opt out completely:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=off \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nPassthrough is idempotent and additive: an image already present in the inner\ndaemon (from a volume, tarball, or earlier run) is skipped, and any single\nimage that fails to copy logs a warning and continues. Like preload, it is\nskipped entirely when `DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1`.\n\n### Scoping to specific images (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`)\n\nThe mode gate decides *whether* an image is safe to pass; the registry allowlist\nnarrows it *by registry host*. `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is one level finer\n— it scopes passthrough to **specific repositories / image names**. When it is\nnon-empty, a host image must match the mode filter **and** at least one\nspace-separated pattern; empty (the default) keeps the mode + registry behavior.\n\nThis is the precise fit for \"seed the inner daemon with only the images I own\"\nrather than every public host image:\n\n```bash\n# Pass through only hive-mind's own images, nothing else on the host:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=public \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=\"konard/hive-mind konard/hive-mind-dind\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\n# Globs and explicit tags / registry-qualified refs also work:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=\"docker.io/konard/hive-mind* konard/hive-mind-dind:latest\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nPatterns are matched against several normalized forms of each host image\nreference, so a bare repository like `konard/hive-mind` matches the tagged\n`konard/hive-mind:latest` and the registry-qualified\n`docker.io/konard/hive-mind:latest` alike. Because it composes with the mode\ngate, `public` mode still refuses a locally-built or private image even when it\nmatches a pattern — the allowlist only ever *narrows* the eligible set, it never\nwidens it past the security filter.\n\nSetting `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is an unambiguous \"I expect these images\npassed through\" signal. So if it is set but **no host socket is mounted**, the\nentrypoint no longer stays silent — it emits a single warning naming the\nmissing `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro` mount, because\nthe nested daemon will otherwise re-pull from the registry on the first\n`docker run` with no hint as to why (issue #102). Plain `box-dind` containers\nthat never set an allowlist still see no extra noise when no socket is mounted.\n\n## Commit Cycles\n\n`DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1` is useful for setup containers where you want to install or\nconfigure files before committing an image:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name box-dind-setup \\\n  -e DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1 \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\ndocker exec box-dind-setup bash -lc 'echo setup complete'\ndocker commit --change 'ENV DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=0' box-dind-setup my-box-dind\ndocker run -d --privileged --name my-box-dind my-box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nThe `--change 'ENV DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=0'` reset is intentional. Docker commit\npreserves container environment, so committing a setup container that has\n`DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1` can produce an image that silently skips dockerd on later\nruns.\n\nCI covers this behavior here:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-commit-cycle.sh\n```\n\n## Sudoers Contract\n\nThe image installs `/etc/sudoers.d/box-dind` with passwordless sudo for only the\nroot operations required by the DIND entrypoint:\n\n```text\n/usr/bin/dockerd\n/usr/bin/chgrp\n/usr/bin/chmod\n/usr/bin/mkdir\n```\n\nDo not broaden this file into general passwordless sudo. If a derived image\nneeds one additional root capability, add a separate sudoers file with the exact\nabsolute binary path and validate it with `visudo`:\n\n```dockerfile\nFROM konard/box-dind\n\nUSER root\nRUN printf '%s\\n' 'box ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/id' \\\n      | install -m 0440 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/sudoers.d/box-dind-example-id && \\\n    visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/box-dind-example-id >/dev/null\n\nUSER box\nENV HOME=/home/box\n```\n\nCI builds and verifies that pattern:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-sudoers-extension.sh\n```\n\n## Storage Driver\n\nWhen `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` is empty, the entrypoint tries `overlay2` if the\nhost advertises overlay support, then `fuse-overlayfs` if it is installed, then\n`vfs`. If a candidate makes `dockerd` exit before it is ready, the entrypoint\nlogs the failure and retries the next candidate. This covers nested runtimes\nwhere overlay support is visible but overlay-backed Docker still cannot start.\n\nUse the default for normal developer workflows. Pin `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs`\nwhen the host cannot run overlay-backed nested Docker reliably or when you need\nthe most conservative compatibility mode. The trade-off is disk use and\nperformance: `vfs` copies whole filesystem trees instead of using overlay\ncopy-on-write layers.\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs \\\n  --name box-dind-vfs \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nBecause that trade-off is easy to hit by accident, the entrypoint emits a\none-time warning whenever the **active** driver ends up being `vfs` — whether\npinned explicitly or reached as the last-resort fallback (issue #104). `vfs`\nstores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's\non-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes — many times\nthe image size — and `docker pull`/`docker run` can fail with `failed to register\nlayer: no space left on device` on a disk far larger than the image. The warning\nmakes that failure traceable instead of looking like a generic \"out of disk\".\n\nIf your host supports it, prefer `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs`: it is\ncopy-on-write **and** works overlay-on-overlay (the compatibility reason `vfs` is\nsometimes chosen), is already shipped in the image, and needs `/dev/fuse`\n(provided by `--privileged`). The warning's remediation line adapts to whether\n`/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it tells you to add `--privileged`\nor `--device /dev/fuse` before switching.\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs \\\n  --name box-dind-cow \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nCI verifies the forced `vfs` path:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh\n```\n\n## Host Prerequisites\n\nThe host kernel and Docker runtime must allow the inner daemon to create the\nmounts, namespaces, cgroups, and networking state that Docker Engine needs.\nIn practice:\n\n- Use `--privileged` for the standard nested Docker mode, or install and use\n  `sysbox-runc` for the Sysbox mode.\n- Do not bind-mount `/var/run/docker.sock` from the host. That switches the\n  model to Docker-outside-of-Docker, exposes host Docker control, and breaks the\n  per-container Docker view.\n- Ensure enough disk is available for `/var/lib/docker`, or mount a volume there.\n- If dockerd does not become ready, inspect `docker logs <container>` and the\n  configured `DIND_LOG_FILE` inside the container before changing timeouts.\n\n## Local Example Runner\n\nTo run the same examples CI runs against a local image:\n\n```bash\ndocker build -f ubuntu/24.04/dind/Dockerfile \\\n  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=konard/box-js:latest \\\n  -t box-dind-js .\n\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-basic-docker-ps.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-commit-cycle.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-sudoers-extension.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh\n```\n\nSet `DIND_KEEP_CONTAINERS=1` while debugging to keep the temporary containers\nand images after a failing example.\n",

[2026-06-19T10:41:03.874Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "# dind-box Usage\n\nThe `-dind` images are regular box images with Docker Engine added. They keep the\nsame user-facing default as the non-dind images: `docker exec` opens as `box`\nwith `HOME=/home/box`. The entrypoint starts the inner `dockerd` with a scoped\npasswordless sudo rule, then hands off to the normal box entrypoint.\n\nThe runnable examples in this document live under `tests/dind/` and are executed\nby pull request CI against the locally built `box-dind-js` image.\n\n## Runtime Flags\n\nUse one of these host-side runtime modes when you need the inner Docker daemon:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged --name box-dind konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --runtime=sysbox-runc --name box-dind konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\n`--privileged` is the default Docker-in-Docker mode. Sysbox is the preferred\nmode for shared hosts when the `sysbox-runc` runtime is installed, because it is\ndesigned for system containers without exposing the host Docker socket.\n\nWithout a runtime that lets the inner daemon create namespaces, mounts, and\ncgroups, the container shell can still start but Docker commands normally fail:\n\n```text\n[dind-entrypoint] WARN: dockerd did not become ready within 30s\nCannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock\n```\n\nThe dockerd log path is controlled by `DIND_LOG_FILE` and defaults to\n`/var/log/dockerd.log`.\n\n## Basic Docker Use\n\nThis example starts the image, waits for the entrypoint to bring up the inner\ndaemon, and checks that `docker exec` still lands as `box`:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged --name box-dind konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\nuntil docker exec box-dind docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do\n  sleep 1\ndone\n\ndocker exec box-dind whoami\ndocker exec box-dind docker ps\ndocker exec box-dind pgrep -x dockerd\n```\n\nCI runs the same flow as an executable example:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-basic-docker-ps.sh\n```\n\n## Runtime Environment\n\nThe entrypoint supports these environment variables:\n\n| Variable | Default | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` | auto | Override the inner dockerd storage driver. |\n| `DIND_DATA_ROOT` | `/var/lib/docker` | Override the inner dockerd data root. |\n| `DIND_LOG_FILE` | `/var/log/dockerd.log` | Write dockerd logs to this path. |\n| `DIND_WAIT_SECONDS` | `30` | Wait this many seconds for dockerd readiness. |\n| `DIND_SKIP_DAEMON` | `0` | Set to `1` to skip dockerd startup. |\n| `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` | _(empty)_ | Space-separated `docker save` tarballs and/or directories of `*.tar` to `docker load` into the nested daemon once it is ready. |\n| `DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES` | _(empty)_ | Space-separated image references to `docker pull` into the nested daemon once it is ready, skipping any that are already present. |\n| `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH` | `public` | Copy images already present on the host into the nested daemon at startup when a host socket is mounted (see below). `public` only passes images with a RepoDigest from an allowlisted public registry; `all` passes every tagged image; `off` disables it. A quiet no-op when no host socket is mounted. |\n| `DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK` | `/var/run/host-docker.sock` | Path inside the container to the mounted *host* Docker socket used for passthrough. Deliberately **not** `/var/run/docker.sock`, so the inner daemon keeps its own isolated socket. |\n| `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES` | common public registries | Space-separated allowlist of registries treated as \"public\" in `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=public` mode (default: `docker.io ghcr.io quay.io gcr.io registry.k8s.io public.ecr.aws mcr.microsoft.com`). |\n| `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` | _(empty)_ | Space-separated allowlist of image references / globs. When non-empty, only host images matching at least one entry are passed through, composed with the mode filter (so `public` still requires a public RepoDigest). Empty keeps the mode + registry filter only. One level finer than `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES` — scope to specific repositories / image names. |\n\nUse a named volume when the inner Docker state should survive container removal:\n\n```bash\ndocker volume create box-dind-data\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v box-dind-data:/var/lib/docker \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\n## Reusing Host Images (Preload)\n\nThe nested daemon starts with an **empty image store**. By default a\n`docker run <image>` *inside* the container reports\n`Unable to find image '<image>' locally` and pulls a fresh copy from the\nregistry — even when the host daemon already has that exact image (issue #94).\nThis is the well-known [Docker-in-Docker image-cache pitfall][jpetazzo].\n\nThe entrypoint can seed the nested daemon at startup so no re-download happens.\n\n### `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` — load `docker save` tarballs (reuse host images)\n\nOn the host, save the image you already have to a tarball, mount it into the\ncontainer, and point `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` at it. The entrypoint loads it with\n`docker load` as soon as the inner daemon is ready, before your workload runs:\n\n```bash\n# Host already has the image; export it without a registry round-trip:\ndocker pull alpine:3.20\ndocker save alpine:3.20 -o /tmp/preload/alpine.tar\n\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /tmp/preload:/preload:ro \\\n  -e DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL=/preload/alpine.tar \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\nuntil docker exec box-dind docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done\n\n# No \"Unable to find image locally\" — it was preloaded, not pulled:\ndocker exec box-dind docker run --rm alpine:3.20 echo hi\n```\n\n`DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` accepts a space-separated list. Any entry that is a\ndirectory loads every `*.tar` file inside it, so you can mount a whole folder of\nsaved images:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /tmp/preload:/preload:ro \\\n  -e DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL=/preload \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nYou can also bake a tarball into a derived image so every container starts warm:\n\n```dockerfile\nFROM konard/box-dind\nUSER root\nCOPY images.tar /opt/preload/images.tar\nENV DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL=/opt/preload/images.tar\nUSER box\nENV HOME=/home/box\n```\n\n### `DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES` — warm the cache from a registry\n\nWhen the source is a registry or pull-through mirror rather than a tarball, list\nthe references in `DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES`. The entrypoint pulls each one after the\ndaemon is ready, but skips any image that is already present (for example one a\nmounted `/var/lib/docker` volume or a `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` already provided):\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES=\"alpine:3.20 busybox:1.36\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nPreload failures are non-fatal: the entrypoint logs a warning and continues so\nthe container shell still starts. Preload is skipped entirely when\n`DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1`, since there is no inner daemon to load into.\n\nCI covers this behavior here:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh\n```\n\n[jpetazzo]: https://jpetazzo.github.io/2015/09/03/do-not-use-docker-in-docker-for-ci/\n\n## Host-Image Passthrough (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH`)\n\n`DIND_PRELOAD_*` above are explicit: you name the tarballs or references to seed.\nPassthrough is the **automatic** counterpart — when you mount the host Docker\nsocket into the container, the entrypoint copies images the host *already has*\ninto the nested daemon at startup, so the inner `docker run` does not re-pull\nthem. It is on by default (`public` mode) but a quiet no-op until a host socket\nis mounted, so the standard `--privileged` run is unchanged.\n\nMount the host socket at `DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK` (default\n`/var/run/host-docker.sock`), read-only:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\nuntil docker exec box-dind docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done\n\n# Public host images were copied into the inner daemon — no re-pull:\ndocker exec box-dind docker images\n```\n\nThe mount path is deliberately **not** `/var/run/docker.sock`. The host socket is\nread only at startup to *seed* images; the inner daemon keeps its own isolated\nsocket and remains the container's runtime. This preserves the per-container\nDocker view from issue #80 — mounting the host socket at the default path would\nswitch the model to Docker-outside-of-Docker and expose host Docker control\n(see [Host Prerequisites](#host-prerequisites)).\n\n### Modes — and why `public` is the default\n\n| Mode | What it copies |\n| --- | --- |\n| `public` _(default)_ | Only host images carrying a `RepoDigest` from an allowlisted public registry (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES`). A RepoDigest proves the image was pulled from that registry and is freely re-pullable, so copying it leaks **no** local build secrets and needs **no** registry credential. Locally-built images (no RepoDigest) and private-registry images are skipped. |\n| `all` | Every tagged host image, including locally-built and private-registry images. Use only when you trust the inner workload with those images. |\n| `off` (also `0`/`false`/`no`) | Disable passthrough entirely. |\n\n```bash\n# Pass through everything the host has, including local builds:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\n# Opt out completely:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=off \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nPassthrough is idempotent and additive: an image already present in the inner\ndaemon (from a volume, tarball, or earlier run) is skipped, and any single\nimage that fails to copy logs a warning and continues. Like preload, it is\nskipped entirely when `DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1`.\n\n### Scoping to specific images (`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`)\n\nThe mode gate decides *whether* an image is safe to pass; the registry allowlist\nnarrows it *by registry host*. `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is one level finer\n— it scopes passthrough to **specific repositories / image names**. When it is\nnon-empty, a host image must match the mode filter **and** at least one\nspace-separated pattern; empty (the default) keeps the mode + registry behavior.\n\nThis is the precise fit for \"seed the inner daemon with only the images I own\"\nrather than every public host image:\n\n```bash\n# Pass through only hive-mind's own images, nothing else on the host:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=public \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=\"konard/hive-mind konard/hive-mind-dind\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\n# Globs and explicit tags / registry-qualified refs also work:\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=\"docker.io/konard/hive-mind* konard/hive-mind-dind:latest\" \\\n  --name box-dind \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nPatterns are matched against several normalized forms of each host image\nreference, so a bare repository like `konard/hive-mind` matches the tagged\n`konard/hive-mind:latest` and the registry-qualified\n`docker.io/konard/hive-mind:latest` alike. Because it composes with the mode\ngate, `public` mode still refuses a locally-built or private image even when it\nmatches a pattern — the allowlist only ever *narrows* the eligible set, it never\nwidens it past the security filter.\n\nSetting `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is an unambiguous \"I expect these images\npassed through\" signal. So if it is set but **no host socket is mounted**, the\nentrypoint no longer stays silent — it emits a single warning naming the\nmissing `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro` mount, because\nthe nested daemon will otherwise re-pull from the registry on the first\n`docker run` with no hint as to why (issue #102). Plain `box-dind` containers\nthat never set an allowlist still see no extra noise when no socket is mounted.\n\n### Verifying the copy actually happened (`issue #106`)\n\nA warning about a forgotten mount only covers one failure mode. Passthrough can\nalso quietly seed *nothing* for other reasons — the host does not have the image\nunder that exact reference, the socket is present but unreachable, or `public`\nmode filtered out a locally-built image (no RepoDigest). In every case the\nentrypoint used to print `image preload/passthrough complete` regardless, and\nthe first nested `docker run` then silently re-pulled the multi-GB image from the\nregistry (~30 GB, ~1 h downstream — `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nSo after passthrough runs, each **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nentry — one with an explicit tag or digest, no glob — is verified to actually be\npresent in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <ref>`). When one is\nmissing, the entrypoint:\n\n- emits a loud, actionable warning naming the un-seeded image(s) and the likely\n  cause (missing/unreachable socket, host lacks that exact ref, or the mode\n  filter dropped it — with the `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` remedy for\n  locally-built/private images), and\n- ends the phase with `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`\n  instead of the misleading `...complete`, so logs never claim success when\n  nothing was copied.\n\nBare repositories (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are not\nconcrete — the host may hold them under any tag — so they are not individually\nverified and never trigger a false alarm. To get this assertion for a specific\nimage, pin it in the allowlist with an explicit tag or digest, e.g.\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6`.\n\n## Commit Cycles\n\n`DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1` is useful for setup containers where you want to install or\nconfigure files before committing an image:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --name box-dind-setup \\\n  -e DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1 \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n\ndocker exec box-dind-setup bash -lc 'echo setup complete'\ndocker commit --change 'ENV DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=0' box-dind-setup my-box-dind\ndocker run -d --privileged --name my-box-dind my-box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nThe `--change 'ENV DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=0'` reset is intentional. Docker commit\npreserves container environment, so committing a setup container that has\n`DIND_SKIP_DAEMON=1` can produce an image that silently skips dockerd on later\nruns.\n\nCI covers this behavior here:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-commit-cycle.sh\n```\n\n## Sudoers Contract\n\nThe image installs `/etc/sudoers.d/box-dind` with passwordless sudo for only the\nroot operations required by the DIND entrypoint:\n\n```text\n/usr/bin/dockerd\n/usr/bin/chgrp\n/usr/bin/chmod\n/usr/bin/mkdir\n```\n\nDo not broaden this file into general passwordless sudo. If a derived image\nneeds one additional root capability, add a separate sudoers file with the exact\nabsolute binary path and validate it with `visudo`:\n\n```dockerfile\nFROM konard/box-dind\n\nUSER root\nRUN printf '%s\\n' 'box ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/id' \\\n      | install -m 0440 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/sudoers.d/box-dind-example-id && \\\n    visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/box-dind-example-id >/dev/null\n\nUSER box\nENV HOME=/home/box\n```\n\nCI builds and verifies that pattern:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-sudoers-extension.sh\n```\n\n## Storage Driver\n\nWhen `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` is empty, the entrypoint tries `overlay2` if the\nhost advertises overlay support, then `fuse-overlayfs` if it is installed, then\n`vfs`. If a candidate makes `dockerd` exit before it is ready, the entrypoint\nlogs the failure and retries the next candidate. This covers nested runtimes\nwhere overlay support is visible but overlay-backed Docker still cannot start.\n\nUse the default for normal developer workflows. Pin `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs`\nwhen the host cannot run overlay-backed nested Docker reliably or when you need\nthe most conservative compatibility mode. The trade-off is disk use and\nperformance: `vfs` copies whole filesystem trees instead of using overlay\ncopy-on-write layers.\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs \\\n  --name box-dind-vfs \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nBecause that trade-off is easy to hit by accident, the entrypoint emits a\none-time warning whenever the **active** driver ends up being `vfs` — whether\npinned explicitly or reached as the last-resort fallback (issue #104). `vfs`\nstores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's\non-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes — many times\nthe image size — and `docker pull`/`docker run` can fail with `failed to register\nlayer: no space left on device` on a disk far larger than the image. The warning\nmakes that failure traceable instead of looking like a generic \"out of disk\".\n\nIf your host supports it, prefer `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs`: it is\ncopy-on-write **and** works overlay-on-overlay (the compatibility reason `vfs` is\nsometimes chosen), is already shipped in the image, and needs `/dev/fuse`\n(provided by `--privileged`). The warning's remediation line adapts to whether\n`/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it tells you to add `--privileged`\nor `--device /dev/fuse` before switching.\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --privileged \\\n  -e DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs \\\n  --name box-dind-cow \\\n  konard/box-dind sleep infinity\n```\n\nCI verifies the forced `vfs` path:\n\n```bash\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh\n```\n\n## Host Prerequisites\n\nThe host kernel and Docker runtime must allow the inner daemon to create the\nmounts, namespaces, cgroups, and networking state that Docker Engine needs.\nIn practice:\n\n- Use `--privileged` for the standard nested Docker mode, or install and use\n  `sysbox-runc` for the Sysbox mode.\n- Do not bind-mount `/var/run/docker.sock` from the host. That switches the\n  model to Docker-outside-of-Docker, exposes host Docker control, and breaks the\n  per-container Docker view.\n- Ensure enough disk is available for `/var/lib/docker`, or mount a volume there.\n- If dockerd does not become ready, inspect `docker logs <container>` and the\n  configured `DIND_LOG_FILE` inside the container before changing timeouts.\n\n## Local Example Runner\n\nTo run the same examples CI runs against a local image:\n\n```bash\ndocker build -f ubuntu/24.04/dind/Dockerfile \\\n  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=konard/box-js:latest \\\n  -t box-dind-js .\n\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-basic-docker-ps.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-commit-cycle.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-sudoers-extension.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh\nDIND_IMAGE=box-dind-js tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh\n```\n\nSet `DIND_KEEP_CONTAINERS=1` while debugging to keep the temporary containers\nand images after a failing example.\n",

For automatic seeding, mount the host socket at `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro` — host-image passthrough is on by default and copies the host's **public** images (those re-pullable from a public registry, so no local secrets or private credentials leak) into the inner daemon; `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` passes everything and `=off` disables it. To copy only specific images rather than every public one, set `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` to a space-separated allowlist of names/globs (e.g. `\"konard/hive-mind konard/hive-mind-dind\"`), composed with the mode filter. The host socket is mounted at a non-default path and read only at startup to seed images, so the inner daemon keeps its own isolated socket. [`latest-arm64`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/pkgs/container/box-rocq-dind?tag=latest-arm64) |\n\n### Docker-in-Docker security model\n\n> ⚠️ **dind-box variants ship a Docker daemon and require elevated privileges to run.**\n>\n> - **Default invocation:** `docker run --privileged konard/box-dind` — the inner `dockerd` needs `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` and access to the kernel's overlay/namespace machinery. Each container has its own daemon, so `docker ps -a` from inside lists only that container's children.\n> - **Recommended secure invocation:** [`docker run --runtime=sysbox-runc konard/box-dind`](https://github.com/nestybox/sysbox) — Sysbox is a drop-in OCI runtime that runs system containers without `--privileged` and without exposing host devices.\n> - **Do NOT bind-mount `/var/run/docker.sock`.** That gives the container root on the host ([Quarkslab](https://blog.quarkslab.com/why-is-exposing-the-docker-socket-a-really-bad-idea.html), [OWASP](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Docker_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html)) and breaks the per-box `docker ps` scoping property.\n> - **Storage:** the inner daemon writes to `/var/lib/docker` inside the container by default. For persistence, mount a volume: `-v box-dind-data:/var/lib/docker`.\n> - **Reusing host images:** the nested daemon starts with an empty image store, so a fresh container re-downloads images the host already has. Seed it explicitly at startup with `DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL` (mount `docker save` tarballs) or `DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES` (pull from a registry/mirror); see [Reusing Host Images](docs/dind/USAGE.md#reusing-host-images-preload). For automatic seeding, mount the host socket at `-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro` — host-image passthrough is on by default and copies the host's **public** images (those re-pullable from a public registry, so no local secrets or private credentials leak) into the inner daemon; `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` passes everything and `=off` disables it. To copy only specific images rather than every public one, set `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` to a space-separated allowlist of names/globs (e.g. `\"konard/hive-mind konard/hive-mind-dind\"`), composed with the mode filter. The host socket is mounted at a non-default path and read only at startup to seed images, so the inner daemon keeps its own isolated socket. See [Host-Image Passthrough](docs/dind/USAGE.md#host-image-passthrough-dind_host_passthrough).\n> - **Usage examples:** see [`docs/dind/USAGE.md`](docs/dind/USAGE.md). Its examples are backed by executable tests under `tests/dind/`.\n\nSee [docs/case-studies/issue-80/CASE-STUDY.md](docs/case-studies/issue-80/CASE-STUDY.md) for the full design and threat model.\n\n## Usage\n\n### Quick Start\n\nPull multi-arch (auto-selects your platform):\n```bash\ndocker pull konard/box:latest\n```\n\nPull specific architecture:\n```bash\n# AMD64\ndocker pull konard/box:latest-amd64\n\n# ARM64 (Apple Silicon, Raspberry Pi, etc.)\ndocker pull konard/box:latest-arm64\n```\n\nPull from GHCR:\n```bash\ndocker pull ghcr.io/link-foundation/box:latest\n```\n\n### Run interactively\n\n```bash\ndocker run -it ghcr.io/link-foundation/box:latest\n```\n\n### Use as base image\n\n```dockerfile\nFROM ghcr.io/link-foundation/box:latest\n\n# Your additional setup here\nCOPY . /home/box\nRUN npm install\n```\n\n### Build locally\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/link-foundation/box.git\ncd box\ndocker build -t box .\n```\n\n## Architecture Support\n\nThe image is built for both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` architectures.\n\n### CI/CD Build Requirements\n\n**IMPORTANT: ARM64 builds MUST use native ARM64 runners.**\n\n| Architecture | Runner | Build Time |\n|-------------|--------|------------|\n| `linux/amd64` | `ubuntu-latest` | ~5-10 minutes |\n| `linux/arm64` | `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (native) | ~30-60 minutes |\n\nNative ARM64 runners provide optimal build performance for compilation-heavy workloads. Emulation would incur a 10-30x performance penalty.\n\nFor detailed analysis, see [Case Study: Issue #7](docs/case-studies/issue-7/README.md).\n\n## Environment\n\nThe container runs as the `box` user with home directory at `/home/box`. `~/.rbenv`\n- Swift: `~/.swift`\n- Lean: `~/.elan`\n- Perl: `~/.perl5`\n- OCaml/Rocq: `~/.opam`\n\n<!-- COMPONENT_SIZES_START -->\n## Component Sizes\n\n_Last updated: 2026-06-05T01:59:41Z_\n\n**Total COMPONENT_SIZES_END -->\n\n## Releasing\n\nReleases are produced by `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which builds and pushes images to **both** the GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) and Docker Hub.\n\nThe workflow uses two sets of credentials:\n\n| Registry | Credential | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| `ghcr.io` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Auto-provisioned by GitHub Actions; no rotation required. |\n| `docker.io` | `secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` + `secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` | Configured at https://github.com/link-foundation/box/settings/secrets/actions. The `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` is a Docker Hub Personal Access Token (PAT). |\n\n### Rotating the Docker Hub PAT\n\nDocker Hub PATs have an immutable expiry (set when the token is created) and **cannot be renewed in place** — they must be re-issued and re-saved as the `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` secret. When the token expires, the release workflow will continue to push to GHCR (since issue #82) but will emit a `::warning` annotation on every build job and skip the Docker Hub portion of the release.\n\nRotation runbook:\n\n1. Sign in to Docker Hub at https://hub.docker.com/settings/security\n2. Click **New Access Token**, scope it to `Read, Write, Delete` for the `konard/box*` repositories, set an expiry that fits the rotation policy (e.g. 90 days), and copy the token.\n3. Open https://github.com/link-foundation/box/settings/secrets/actions and update `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`.\n4. Re-run the most recent failed release run, or push an empty commit, or trigger `workflow_dispatch` on `Build and Release Docker Image` with `release_mode=release-only` to re-publish the current `VERSION` to Docker Hub.\n\nSee [`docs/case-studies/issue-82/CASE-STUDY.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-82/CASE-STUDY.md) for the incident that introduced this hardening.\n\n## Documentation\n\n- [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) - System architecture and design decisions\n- [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) - Project requirements and constraints\n- [docs/case-studies/](docs/case-studies/) - Case studies and incident analysis\n\n## License\n\nMIT License - see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.\n",

This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. [2026-06-19T10:44:53.597Z] [INFO]   ✅ Found pull request #107: "box-dind: verify host-image passthrough seeded the nested daemon and stop falsely reporting 'complete' (issue #106)"
[2026-06-19T10:44:54.070Z] [STDOUT] ## Problem (issue #106)

box-dind's nested Docker daemon kept re-downloading multi-GB host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) on the first nested `docker run` **even with `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` set**, while the entrypoint still printed `image preload/passthrough complete`. A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).

The issue asked for three code-level fixes:
1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print "complete" when nothing was copied.
2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.
3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).

## Fix

The root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.

- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.
- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.
- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.
- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.

## How to reproduce / verify

- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest "complete", no warning; concrete absent → loud "did NOT seed" warning + "finished WITH WARNINGS", no "complete"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**
- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, "complete", no "did NOT seed") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → "did NOT seed expected image(s)…", "finished WITH WARNINGS", "complete" absent).

## Docs

- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new "Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.
- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false "complete").

## Versioning

Added `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). VERSION is bumped automatically by CI on merge.
