Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

[2026-06-19T11:04:09.140Z] [STDOUT] {"name":"main","commit":{"sha":"4ad**********************************aa5","node_id":"C_kwDOQ2-R2doAKDRhZGQ1MWRmYzBjMTRjNmJjMDgwNDkzZmRkZmIyNmFiNjE4NzhhYTU","commit":{"author":{"name":"github-actions[bot]","email":"github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-06-15T06:52:26Z"},"committer":{"name":"github-actions[bot]","email":"github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-06-15T06:52:26Z"},"message":"2.3.3: CI reliability: retry transient network failures in the JS image build and remove a SIGPIPE false-negative from the dind example tests (issue #104 / PR #105). The JS image build (`ubuntu/24.04/js/install.sh`, `COPY`'d into every dind/language image) occasionally died on a single transient third-party error, with no retry: the lean/language build hit a flaky npm registry response during `npm install -g npm@latest`, and the dind-swift build hit `playwright install … msedge …` getting an invalid GPG key body from packages.microsoft.com (\"gpg: no valid OpenPGP data found\" → \"Failed to install msedge\"). Every network-bound build step — the npm self-update, the Playwright/Puppeteer CLI install, and the Playwright browser-binary download — now goes through a `run_with_retry` wrapper that retries with exponential backoff (mirroring `apt_update_with_retry` in `common.sh`, with the same overridable retry budget so it stays unit-testable). `playwright install` skips already-present browsers, so a retry only re-attempts the one that blipped. This is build-time resilience only — the resulting image is unchanged on success. Separately, the dind example suite asserted on container logs with `docker logs … | grep -q \"needle\"`. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image pres

When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}
