This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

A misconfigured deployment — forgotten host-socket mount, host missing that exact ref, or the `mode=public` filter dropping a locally-built/private image — therefore looked perfectly healthy right up until the slow re-pull. This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image present → honest \"complete\", no warning; concrete absent → loud \"did NOT seed\" warning + \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", no \"complete\"; glob/bare entries never false-alarm; `ref_is_concrete` classification. **62 passed, 0 failed.**\n- `tests/dind/example-preload-images.sh` (runs in CI on the `js` variant, `--privileged`): new `verify_ok` case (concrete allowlist + socket mounted, `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all` → image present, \"complete\", no \"did NOT seed\") and `verify_miss` case (concrete allowlist, **no** socket → \"did NOT seed expected image(s)…\", \"finished WITH WARNINGS\", \"complete\" absent).\n\n## Docs\n\n- `docs/dind/USAGE.md`: new \"Verifying the copy actually happened (issue #106)\" subsection + updated `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` env-var row.\n- `README.md`: verification clause on the host-image-reuse note (pin a concrete tag/digest; loud warning instead of false \"complete\").\n\n## Versioning\n\nAdded `.changeset/issue-106-passthrough-verify.md` (`bump: patch`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); The JS image build (`ubuntu/24.04/js/install.sh`, `COPY`'d into every dind/language image) occasionally died on a single transient third-party error, with no retry: the lean/language build hit a flaky npm registry response during `npm install -g npm@latest`, and the dind-swift build hit `playwright install … msedge …` getting an invalid GPG key body from packages.microsoft.com (\"gpg: no valid OpenPGP data found\" → \"Failed to install msedge\"). Every network-bound build step — the npm self-update, the Playwright/Puppeteer CLI install, and the Playwright browser-binary download — now goes through a `run_with_retry` wrapper that retries with exponential backoff (mirroring `apt_update_with_retry` in `common.sh`, with the same overridable retry budget so it stays unit-testable). `playwright install` skips already-present browsers, so a retry only re-attempts the one that blipped. This is build-time resilience only — the resulting image is unchanged on success. Separately, the dind example suite asserted on container logs with `docker logs … | grep -q \"needle\"`. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Observe wall-clock (~1 hour) and disk delta (`df -h` before/after shows ~30 GB\n   consumed inside the container's data-root).\n3. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); if\n   absent, surface it instead of proceeding to a silent re-pull.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist) in the\n   box-dind README and in the hive-mind deployment so operators get passthrough\n   by default.\n\n## References\n\n- box #94 (empty nested image store → re-download) — closed, symptom persists.\n- box #102 (silent passthrough no-op) — closed, symptom persists.\n- Downstream report: link-assistant/hive-mind #1914 and #1946 (full case study\n  with evidence and screenshots).\n","closed_by":null,"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/link-foundation/box/issues/106/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":null,"pinned_comment":null}

This is the recurring production symptom behind already-closed issues #94 and #102 (still observed downstream in `link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`/`#1946`).\n\nThe issue asked for three code-level fixes:\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** — never print \"complete\" when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy** — after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is actually present in the nested daemon.\n3. **Document the required deployment wiring** (socket mount + allowlist).\n\n## Fix\n\nThe root-cause robust catch-all is **verification**, which subsumes fix #1: any silent no-op path (no socket, unreachable socket, host lacks the ref, mode filter drop, or a `save|load` failure) leaves a named allowlist image missing → loud warning + an honest terminal marker.\n\n- **`verify_passthrough_images()`** (new): after `preload_tarballs`/`passthrough_host_images`/`preload_images`, for every **concrete** `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` entry it runs `docker image inspect` against the nested daemon. Missing images produce a loud, actionable warning that distinguishes the two failure modes (host socket reachable but lacks the ref / dropped by `mode=public`, vs. no usable socket mounted) and names the remediation.\n- **`ref_is_concrete()`** (new): only entries with an explicit tag or `@sha256:` digest are verified. Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. The re-pull still happens naturally; the loud warning is the explicit signal.\n\n## How to reproduce / verify\n\n- `experiments/preload-unit-test.sh` (source-only mode): new cases — concrete image pres

Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. box-dind: nested daemon still re-downloads host images (~30 GB, ~1 hour) despite passthrough — continuation of #94 / #102\n\n## Summary\n\nWhen `solve`/`hive` runs inside `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` (docker-in-docker),\nthe nested Docker daemon starts with an **empty image store** and re-pulls the\nmulti-GB image that the **host already has**, instead of reusing it via\npassthrough. On a recent run this cost ~30 GB of download and ~1 hour of\nwall-clock before the actual task started.\n\nThis is the same defect tracked in #94 (\"nested daemon starts with empty image\nstore, forcing re-download of host images\") and #102 (\"silent no-op when\n`DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is set but no host socket is mounted\"), both\nclosed, but the symptom still reproduces in production with box-dind 2.0.6.\n\n## Environment\n\n```\nimage: konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6\nHIVE_MIND_IMAGE_VARIANT=dind\ndocker: 29.5.3\nstart-command: 0.29.1 (detached docker launch)\n```\n\nThe dind entrypoint reports passthrough \"complete\", yet the image is still pulled\nfresh:\n\n```\n[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)\n[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s\n[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete   <-- claims complete…\n```\n\n…but the overall run still took ~54 minutes and consumed ~30 GB, consistent with\na full re-pull of the dind image inside the nested daemon.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Launch a detached docker session using the dind variant on a host that already\n   has `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6` pulled.\n2. Note the entrypoint prints `image preload/passthrough complete` even though no\n   host image was actually copied into the nested store.\n\n## Expected\n\nThe nested daemon should reuse the host's already-present image (via the\ndocumented passthrough: host docker socket mount + `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES`\nallowlist), so no multi-GB re-download occurs and startup is seconds, not an hour.\n\n## Workaround\n\nMount the host docker socket read-only and set the allowlist so passthrough can\nactually copy the image:\n\n```\ndocker run ... \\\n  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/host-docker.sock:ro \\\n  -e DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES=konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 \\\n  konard/hive-mind-dind:2.0.6 ...\n```\n\n## Suggested fix (code level)\n\n1. **Fail loudly, not silently** (re #102): if `DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES` is\n   set but no host docker socket is mounted/reachable, the entrypoint must log a\n   clear error and either abort or fall back to pull with an explicit warning —\n   never print `image preload/passthrough complete` when nothing was copied.\n2. **Verify the copy**: after passthrough, assert the allowlisted image is\n   actually present in the nested daemon (`docker image inspect <name>`); Bare repos (`konard/hive-mind`) and globs (`konard/hive-mind*`) are skipped to avoid false alarms (the host may hold them under any tag). A `:` is treated as a tag separator only in the last path segment, so a registry port like `host:5000/repo` is correctly non-concrete.\n- The terminal line is now honest: `image preload/passthrough complete` **only** when every concrete allowlisted image is actually present; otherwise `image preload/passthrough finished WITH WARNINGS`.\n- **No auto-pull fallback** — that would mask the config error and incur the same multi-GB download. Every network-bound build step — the npm self-update, the Playwright/Puppeteer CLI install, and the Playwright browser-binary download — now goes through a `run_with_retry` wrapper that retries with exponential backoff (mirroring `apt_update_with_retry` in `common.sh`, with the same overridable retry budget so it stays unit-testable). `playwright install` skips already-present browsers, so a retry only re-attempts the one that blipped. This is build-time resilience only — the resulting image is unchanged on success. Separately, the dind example suite asserted on container logs with `docker logs … | grep -q \"needle\"`. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in `docs/dind/USAGE.md`.\n---\nOn branch issue-106-81bf2d7bb66f\nYour branch is up to date with 'origin/issue-106-81bf2d7bb66f'.\n\nnothing to commit, working tree clean",

(issue #106)\n526\tverify_passthrough_images() {\n527\t  host_passthrough_enabled || return 0\n528\t  [ -n \"$DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES\" ] || return 0\n529\t\n530\t  missing=\"\"\n531\t  for entry in $DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES; do\n532\t    ref_is_concrete \"$entry\" || continue\n533\t    if ! Overridable so the unit\n# test can exercise both the \"present\" and \"missing\" remediation branches without\n# a real device node; in production it is always /dev/fuse.\nDIND_FUSE_DEVICE=\"${DIND_FUSE_DEVICE:-/dev/fuse}\"\n\n# When the active storage driver is vfs, emit a one-time warning explaining the\n# copy-on-write footgun. vfs is a safe last-resort fallback (and a legitimate\n# explicit pin for overlay-on-overlay compatibility), so this is observability,\n# not a default change: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy,\n# so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the SUM of all cumulative layer\n# sizes — many times the image size — and 'docker pull'/'docker run' can fail with\n# 'failed to register layer: no space left on device' on a disk far larger than\n# the image. Without this breadcrumb the generic disk error is easily misdiagnosed\n# as \"not enough disk\" instead of \"wrong driver wastes the disk\"\n# (link-assistant/hive-mind#1914). The remediation depends on whether the\n# copy-on-write fuse-overlayfs driver's device node is available. (issue #104)\nwarn_if_vfs_storage_driver() {\n  [ \"$1\" = \"vfs\" ] || return 0\n\n  warn \"dockerd is using the 'vfs' storage driver, which has NO copy-on-write:\"\n  warn \"every image layer is stored as a full copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk\"\n  warn \"footprint becomes the SUM of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the\"\n  warn \"image size). Returns\n# non-zero (so passthrough is a quiet no-op) when no host socket is present or\n# the socket cannot be reached.\nhost_docker_available() {\n  [ -n \"$DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK\" ] || return 1\n  [ -S \"$DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK\" ] || return 1\n  docker -H \"unix://$DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK\" version >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1\n  return 0\n}\n\n# Extract the registry host from an image reference or repo-digest. Docker Hub\n# refs (\"alpine\", \"library/alpine\", \"user/repo\") have no host component and map\n# to docker.io. A first path segment containing '.' or ':' (or \"localhost\") is\n# treated as an explicit registry host.\nimage_registry() {\n  first=\"${1%%/*}\"\n  case \"$first\" in\n    localhost|*.*|*:*) printf '%s\\n' \"$first\" ;;\n    *) printf '%s\\n' \"docker.io\" ;;\n  esac\n}\n\nregistry_is_public() {\n  for allowed in $DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_REGISTRIES; do\n    [ \"$1\" = \"$allowed\" ] && return 0\n  done\n  return 1\n}\n\n# When DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES is non-empty, a host image is eligible only\n# if its reference matches at least one space-separated pattern (shell glob).\n# Patterns are matched against several normalized forms of the reference so that\n# an entry like \"konard/hive-mind\" matches \"konard/hive-mind:latest\" and the\n# docker.io-qualified \"docker.io/konard/hive-mind[:latest]\" alike, keeping the\n# allowlist ergonomic. An empty list always passes (filter disabled). (issue #97)\nhost_image_matches_images_filter() {\n  ref=\"$1\"\n  [ -n \"$DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES\" ] || return 0\n\n  repo=\"${ref%:*}\"   # strip the :tag -> repository (handles host:port/path too)\n\n  # Candidate forms to test patterns against: the tagged ref, the bare repo, and\n  # — for Docker Hub refs — the same two with an explicit docker.io/ prefix (or,\n  # if already docker.io-qualified, with that prefix stripped).\n  set -- \"$ref\" \"$repo\"\n  case \"$ref\" in\n    docker.io/*)\n      set -- \"$@\" \"${ref#docker.io/}\" \"${repo#docker.io/}\" ;;\n    *)\n      if [ \"$(image_registry \"$ref\")\" = \"docker.io\" ]; then\n        set -- \"$@\" \"docker.io/$ref\" \"docker.io/$repo\"\n      fi ;;\n  esac\n\n  for pattern in $DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES; do\n    for cand in \"$@\"; do\n      # shellcheck disable=SC2254  # intentional glob match against the pattern\n      case \"$cand\" in\n        $pattern) return 0 ;;\n      esac\n    done\n  done\n  return 1\n}\n\n# Decide whether a host image should be passed through under the current mode.\n# \"all\"    -> every tagged image qualifies.\n# \"public\" -> the image must carry a RepoDigest from an allowlisted public\n#             registry, proving it was pulled from a public registry and is\n#             freely re-pullable. Locally-built images (no RepoDigest) and\n#             private-registry images are excluded, so passthrough never copies\n#             local build secrets or images that required a credential.\nhost_image_passes_filter() {\n  ref=\"$1\"; repo_digests=\"$2\"\n\n  # Repository/name allowlist, composed with the mode gate below: when set, the\n  # image must additionally match at least one pattern. (issue #97)\n  host_image_matches_images_filter \"$ref\" || return 1\n\n  case \"$DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH\" in\n    all) return 0 ;;\n    public)\n      [ -n \"$repo_digests\" ] || return 1\n      for rd in $repo_digests; do\n        if registry_is_public \"$(image_registry \"${rd%@*}\")\"; then\n          return 0\n        fi\n      done\n      return 1 ;;\n    *) return 1 ;;\n  esac\n}\n\npassthrough_host_images() {\n  host_passthrough_enabled || return 0\n\n  if ! host_docker_available; then\n    if [ -n \"$DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK\" ] && [ -e \"$DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK\" ]; then\n      # A socket file exists but is unreachable: surface it.\n      warn \"host docker socket at ${DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK} is not accessible; skipping passthrough\"\n    elif [ -n \"$DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES\" ]; then\n      # Operator opted in via an allowlist but no host socket is mounted: the\n      # nested daemon will NOT be seeded and the first nested 'docker run' will\n      # re-pull from the registry. A bare repository\n# (\"konard/hive-mind\") or a glob (\"konard/hive-mind*\") is NOT concrete — it has\n# no single deterministic ref to inspect in the nested daemon (the host may hold\n# it under any tag), so verification skips it rather than risk a false alarm.\n# Note: a ':' is only a tag separator in the LAST path segment; \"host:5000/repo\"\n# is a registry port, not a tag, and is correctly treated as non-concrete.\nref_is_concrete() {\n  case \"$1\" in\n    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*) return 1 ;;   # glob pattern\n  esac\n  case \"$1\" in\n    *@*) return 0 ;;                 # explicit digest (…@sha256:…)\n  esac\n  case \"${1##*/}\" in\n    *:*) return 0 ;;                 # explicit tag in the final segment\n  esac\n  return 1\n}\n\n# Assert that every concrete DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES entry actually landed\n# in the nested daemon after passthrough ran. (issue #106)\nverify_passthrough_images() {\n  host_passthrough_enabled || return 0\n  [ -n \"$DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES\" ] || return 0\n\n  missing=\"\"\n  for entry in $DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH_IMAGES; do\n    ref_is_concrete \"$entry\" || continue\n    if ! docker image inspect \"$entry\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n      missing=\"${missing:+$missing }$entry\"\n    fi\n  done\n\n  [ -n \"$missing\" ] || return 0\n\n  warn \"host-image passthrough did NOT seed expected image(s) into the nested daemon: ${missing}\"\n  warn \"the first nested 'docker run' will re-pull each from its registry (multi-GB, slow).\"\n  if host_docker_available; then\n    warn \"the host socket at ${DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK} is reachable, so the host most likely does not\"\n    warn \"have the image under that exact reference, or mode=${DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH} filtered it out\"\n    warn \"(public passes only images with a public RepoDigest; use DIND_HOST_PASSTHROUGH=all for\"\n    warn \"locally-built or private images).\"\n  else\n    warn \"no usable host docker socket at ${DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK}; mount it read-only with\"\n    warn \"-v /var/run/docker.sock:${DIND_HOST_DOCKER_SOCK}:ro so passthrough can copy the image.\"\n  fi\n  return 1\n}\n\npreload_into_daemon() {\n  # Tarball/registry preload only run when their vars are set; host passthrough\n  # is on by default, so we still proceed to give it a chance to find a socket.\n  if [ -z \"$DIND_PRELOAD_TARBALL\" ] && [ -z \"$DIND_PRELOAD_IMAGES\" ] \\\n     && ! host_passthrough_enabled; then\n    return 0\n  fi\n\n  if ! docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    warn \"Skipping image preload/passthrough because the nested dockerd is not ready\"\n    return 0\n  fi\n\n  preload_tarballs\n  passthrough_host_images\n  preload_images\n  # Emit a terminal marker once every preload path has finished so consumers\n  # (and tests) can synchronize on \"images are seeded\" rather than racing the\n  # asynchronous load against mere dockerd readiness. Every network-bound build step — the npm self-update, the Playwright/Puppeteer CLI install, and the Playwright browser-binary download — now goes through a `run_with_retry` wrapper that retries with exponential backoff (mirroring `apt_update_with_retry` in `common.sh`, with the same overridable retry budget so it stays unit-testable). `playwright install` skips already-present browsers, so a retry only re-attempts the one that blipped. This is build-time resilience only — the resulting image is unchanged on success. Separately, the dind example suite asserted on container logs with `docker logs … | grep -q \"needle\"`. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` closes the pipe the instant it matches, which can deliver SIGPIPE to the still-streaming `docker logs`; pipefail then propagates that 141 and a present message reads as absent, failing the test spuriously (observed on the preload test even though the expected line was right there in the logs). `tests/dind/lib.sh` now provides a pipe-free `logs_contain` helper (capture once, match with a `case` glob) and all example assertions use it. Covered by new unit tests `experiments/test-issue104-build-retry.sh` and `experiments/test-issue104-logs-contain.sh`.; dind-box: warn when the nested daemon runs on the `vfs` storage driver (issue #104). When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in `docs/dind/USAGE.md`.\n--- merge-base check ---\nmain IS ancestor (up to date)",

When the inner dockerd ends up on `vfs` — either pinned explicitly via `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=vfs` (e.g. for overlay-on-overlay compatibility) or reached as the last-resort auto-detect fallback — large images could fail to pull/run with a cryptic `failed to register layer: no space left on device` and **no hint** that the storage driver was the cause. `vfs` performs no copy-on-write: it stores every image layer as a full, independent copy, so a multi-GB image's on-disk footprint becomes the *sum* of all cumulative layer sizes (many times the image size), and a >30 GB image can overflow a disk with far more than 30 GB free (`link-assistant/hive-mind#1914`). This is observability, not a default change — `vfs` stays the safe fallback. The entrypoint now emits a single, actionable warning right after the daemon becomes ready whenever the active driver is `vfs`, explaining the copy-on-write/disk implication and naming the `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER=fuse-overlayfs` remediation (copy-on-write, works overlay-on-overlay, already shipped in the image). The remediation line adapts to whether `/dev/fuse` is present, so when it is missing it points at `--privileged` / `--device /dev/fuse` first. The `DIND_STORAGE_DRIVER` doc comment now spells out the `vfs` disk amplification too. Covered by a new unit test (`experiments/test-issue104-vfs-warning.sh`) and a new assertion in the CI-run `tests/dind/example-storage-driver-vfs.sh`; documented in `docs/dind/USAGE.md`.\n--- merge-base check ---\nmain IS ancestor (up to date)",
